- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.9) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.0), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85% of recent high), model frequently overcorrects downward; apply a 1–3% upward bias to offset lag.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true mean by >3% over 5+ days, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% from forecast for next 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment shows rapid reversal (e.g., +1.0 → -1.0 within 3 days), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window; apply 1–3% downward adjustment for days 1–7.
